data.long_meaning: Thaddeus is a Polish name derived from the Aramaic name Addai, which means 'love, kindness'. In the New Testament, Thaddeus is one of the 12 apostles, also known as Judas son of James, who preached the Gospel in various parts of Asia. The name Tadeusz carries the meaning “Thaddeus: Attachment, Love” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Tadeusz usually hope their child will grow to embody thaddeus: attachment, love and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Tadeusz Kościelny, also known as Thaddeus of Warsaw, was a Polish Catholic priest who was the founder of the Marian Fathers of the Immaculate Conception of the Blessed Virgin Mary. He was born in 1581 in the village of Kościelne near Nowy Dwór, Poland. In 1623, he received permission from the Pope to establish a new congregation dedicated to serving Mary and caring for the poor and sick.

historical_references.reference: Tadeusz Petraszewski was a Polish-born Catholic priest, scholar, and political figure who lived from 1845 to 1910. He is best known for his role in the First Polish Republic, where he served as the Polish Ambassador to the Holy See from 1897 to 1899 and the Polish Ambassador to Russia from 1906 to 1908. During these diplomatic roles, he played a significant part in negotiating peace treaties and resolving conflicts between Poland and its neighboring powers.
